Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion

Class QuestNavPoseSource

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion.PoseSource
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.fusion.QuestNavPoseSource
public class QuestNavPoseSource extends PoseSource
A Meta Quest running QuestNav as a pose source.

It wraps the vendordep's QuestNav: it consumes the unread frames, undoes the mounting transform to go from the headset pose to the robot pose, and discards anything that arrives without valid tracking.

A VIO is not a camera

There are no tags, no distance and no ambiguity: a VIO's error does not depend on how far it is from anything, but on how long it has gone without being corrected. That is why the default strategy is StdDevStrategies.vioTimeDrift(double, double, double, double), and why you have to call notifyPoseReset() when the robot sends a setPose to the headset: that is where the real drift goes back to zero, and the strategy has to hear about it.

It keeps the newest frame

The headset publishes at 100 Hz and the robot runs at 50, so every cycle has two or more frames pending. The last one with valid tracking is used. Feeding them all to the estimator would not be wrong either, but the newest already contains the information of the earlier ones and costs half as much.

The timestamp warning

In simulation, if SimulatedQuestNav publishes on the same NetworkTables instance the robot consumes, PoseFrame.dataTimestamp() is a constant 1 microsecond. This source detects that and warns once instead of feeding the pose estimator measurements dated to year zero, which is exactly the silent failure worth avoiding. The fix is to switch on withNetworkClient(true) in the simulator.

      public QuestNavPoseSource withRequireTracking(boolean enabled)
      Controls whether frames without valid tracking are discarded. Switching it off is almost never a good idea: during a tracking loss the headset repeats the last good pose, which very soon stops describing where the robot is.
      Parameters:
      enabled - true to require tracking.
      Returns:
      this same source.

    • notifyPoseReset

      public void notifyPoseReset()
      Signals that the headset has just been re-anchored and its drift went back to zero.

      Call it right after questNav.setPose(...). Without this the drift strategy keeps inflating the uncertainty forever and the estimator ends up ignoring a sensor that has just become perfect.

    • resetPose

      public void resetPose(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose2d robotPose)

    • telemetryDetail

      protected String telemetryDetail()
      Description copied from class: PoseSource
      A free-form detail the subclass can publish alongside the status.

      It exists so RejectionReason.NO_MEASUREMENT is not a dead end: "the source reported nothing" could mean the camera sees no tags, the headset is disconnected, or the timestamp is unusable, and from the dashboard all three look the same.

      Overrides:
      telemetryDetail in class PoseSource
      Returns:
